**Johnson & Johnson had the higher net margin in fiscal 2023, by about 37.7 percentage points.**

| Company | Revenue | Net income | Net margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Johnson & Johnson | ~$85.16B | ~$35.15B | ~41.3% |
| Pfizer | ~$58.50B | ~$2.12B (attributable to Pfizer) | ~3.6% |

These figures are from my recollection of the fiscal 2023 10-Ks, not checked against the filings, so treat them as approximate.

The gap is unusually wide for two reasons:
- **J&J's net income includes discontinued operations.** About $21B of it is a one-time gain from separating Kenvue. On continuing operations alone, J&J's margin would be roughly 16%.
- **Pfizer's earnings fell sharply.** COVID product revenue declined and Pfizer took large write-offs.
